target.title: fix(memory): hide QMD transport metadata from recalled content
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

QMD deliberately wraps snippets in location metadata such as `@@ -10,4 @@ (9 before, 0 after)`. Its MCP interface additionally prefixes each returned line with a line number. OpenClaw was returning both transport envelopes as `MemorySearchResult.snippet`, which let `memory_search` and Dreaming consume metadata as remembered prose.

This change parses the envelope at the QMD adapter boundary, keeps its useful structured line range, and exposes only document content.

Related: #106937
Related: #89444, #71030

## Why

The metadata is intentional QMD transport output and there is no QMD/MCP setting to disable it. Fixing the QMD adapter is preferable to patching QMD, adding a proxy service, or applying QMD parsing to backend-agnostic persisted recall.

The parser is deliberately conservative:

- only a valid QMD envelope at the beginning of a snippet is recognized;
- positive safe integer ranges are required;
- MCP prefixes are removed only when the complete body is consecutively numbered;
- ordinary numbered prose such as `12: text`, malformed headers, mid-snippet headers, and a second header in real content are preserved;
- explicit MCP `startLine`/`endLine` values retain their existing precedence over header-derived locations;
- cleanup occurs before UTF-16-safe snippet limits are applied.

Historical recall-store migration is intentionally out of scope. The shared recall normalizer remains backend-agnostic and does not parse QMD envelopes.

## User Impact

- `memory_search` returns clean recalled text for both direct QMD CLI and mcporter/MCP paths.
- Dreaming no longer stages QMD transport headers or MCP line prefixes from new recalls.
- Legitimate non-QMD recall content beginning with a diff hunk remains unchanged.
- Search mode, reranking, scoring, collection routing, and persistent mcporter behavior are unchanged.

## Live Real-Environment Proof

Proof head: `5714bf96da5c3f15184f267c270d19dfd2018a73`

Environment: Node `v22.23.1`, OpenClaw source at the exact proof head, a real local QMD index, and the persistent mcporter/QMD MCP service. Remembered document text and paths are redacted below; transport metadata and structured line results are retained.

### Direct QMD CLI

The real direct QMD query returned this raw transport shape:

```text
@@ -2,4 @@ (1 before, 53 after)
[document content redacted]
```

The patched `QmdMemoryManager` with `mcporter.enabled=false` returned:

```json
{
  "startLine": 2,
  "endLine": 5,
  "snippet": "[clean document content redacted]"
}
```

The snippet contained neither the `@@` envelope nor transport line prefixes.

### mcporter/MCP

The same real index through the persistent `mcporter call qmd.query` transport returned the numbered MCP envelope:

```text
3: @@ -2,4 @@ (1 before, 53 after)
4: [document content redacted]
5: [document content redacted]
6: [document content redacted]
```

The patched `QmdMemoryManager` with `mcporter.enabled=true` returned:

```json
{
  "startLine": 2,
  "endLine": 5,
  "snippet": "[clean document content redacted]"
}
```

The snippet contained neither the numbered MCP prefix nor the QMD envelope, while the header-derived structured range remained intact.

### Stored-Recall Safety

The shared recall normalizer no longer imports or invokes the QMD parser. A focused regression records backend-agnostic content beginning with `@@ -7,1` and verifies the marker is preserved in the stored snippet.

Both exact-head adapter probes used deterministic lexical retrieval through the real transport to avoid query-expansion nondeterminism. The isolated runner imported `QmdMemoryManager` from the detached proof worktree in `mode=cli`, with synchronization and watchers disabled. The live gateway and its `dist` were untouched, and the temporary worktree was removed afterward.

## Validation

Validated on the exact proof head above:

- Exact-head GitHub CI build: passed.
- `qmd-snippet.test.ts`: 13/13 passed.
- Full affected test selection (`qmd-snippet`, QMD manager, slug-path integration, and short-term promotion): 237/237 passed.
- Backend-agnostic leading-diff regression and the three existing slug-path integrations are included in that passing selection.
- Changed files: `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Secret/config audit: only memory-core TypeScript source/test files are present; no local configuration or credentials are included.

## AI Assistance

This patch was implemented with Codex assistance. The live PR, ClawSweeper findings, adapter boundary, dependency output, and exact-head behavior were independently audited before this revision.

Maintainers may edit this branch.
